aerodynamic: Rounded radius → smoother flow, gentle stall
Smooth curvature avoids sudden pressure spikes
manufacturability: Extremely sharp edges are hard to machine or mold accurately
Minimum practical radius ~0.5% to 3% of chord

aerodynamic: Thick/blunt → higher drag, possible vortex shedding
manufacturability: Minimum practical thickness ~0.25% to 1% of chord for durability

aerodynamic: More camber → higher lift at low AoA
Camber distribution along chord affects lift curve and pitching moment
manufacturability: Extreme camber changes difficult to machine or cast
Recommended maximum camber ~3% to 6% of chord for general aircraft airfoils

aerodynamic: Maximum thickness location influences lift and stall behavior
manufacturability: Very thin profiles (<6% chord) are fragile and hard to produce
Typical maximum thickness ~12% to 18% of chord for general aviation airfoils
Symmetrical shapes are simpler to mold or machine

aerodynamic: Rapid taper → lower drag but may affect stall
manufacturability: Avoid taper angles >10° for easier tooling

aerodynamic: Abrupt kinks or roughness → early transition, separation, higher drag
manufacturability: Maintain smooth curves without sharp steps
Roughness height <0.05% of chord recommended for laminar airfoils

aerodynamic: Thickness and curvature must balance lift, drag, and moment requirements
manufacturability: Ensure minimum thickness ≥3% of chord for structural integrity
Avoid sharp internal angles or deep concave surfaces

practical_fabrication_tips: Keep curvature changes gradual for easier tooling
Ensure minimum thickness is sufficient for structural integrity
Favor surfaces that can be consistently reproduced with available manufacturing methods (CNC, molding, composite layup)
quick_visual_rule_of_thumb: Rounded, smooth leading edge + moderate camber (~3–6%) + gentle thickness taper (~12–18% chord) → aerodynamically efficient and easier to manufacture
Extreme thin edges, abrupt curvature, or unusual camber spikes → may perform well theoretically but are difficult and costly to produce
